'We can see no valid ground for assuming that the said amendment was contrary to the Constitution' - challenge was only to the 1969 amendment of s.7 empowering magistrates to sentence for s.296 offences, so partial not total

'We do not see any reason why this approach should not be applied to the mandatory sentence of death specified by section 296 (2)' then remits for resentencing; same pattern as E11 (Muruatetu applied by parity = read_down)

para 34 'the elements constituting the defence should be read disjunctively if the two sub-sections are to make sense': ordinary statutory construction of 8(5), not a constitutional narrowing (it widens the defence) - interpreted, not read_down
para 11 quotes SC Mwangi then 'We are bound by the decision of the Supreme Court'; para 13 constitutional point 'does not therefore fall for our determination'
para 11 'to the extent of finding that the mandatory nature of the sentence of life imprisonment provided under Section 8(2)... is unconstitutional'; matches E12 Manyeso type
para 23 'the powers vested under section 166 of the CPC is unconstitutional'; para 24 limits it to 'the powers given to the President to order detention' - partial

para 31 relies on SC Mwangi; para 32 'both courts below correctly imposed the death sentence as prescribed by law': no constitutional challenge decided, just applies the section

para 16 'We have addressed our minds to the issue of death sentence being unconstitutional... it remains the mandatory sentence as under section 296(2)'; row fills subsection 296(2) yet scope=total - should be partial

para 53(c) 'A declaration that section 333(2) applies to the original sentence as well as the sentence imposed during resentencing'

para 153(b) covers 167(1)(a),(b),(2),(3),(4) - partial
